cases.doc:
A new YT seizure was attempted while this escrow instance already holds an unfinalized YT
record. YT's yield accounting is pooled by this escrow's own holding *address*, not per
`RecoveryRecord` -- so two unfinalized YT records held at once would both accrue against
the same shared pending-claim bucket, and whichever is `finalize_record`'d first would
drain yield that was actually accruing against the *other* record too. Total funds stay
conserved, but per-record attribution would be wrong, which matters for a compliance/legal
recovery trail. Rather than a full per-record proportional-yield redesign, this prevents
the unsafe state from ever occurring: finalize the outstanding YT record first. Found
during audit review. PT-only seizures are unaffected -- PT has no pooled yield accounting.
cases.name: UnfinalizedYtRecordExists

void_v0.doc: Present (holding that record's id) whenever this escrow currently holds an unfinalized YT\nrecord; absent otherwise. At most one at a time -- see `Error::UnfinalizedYtRecordExists`.
void_v0.name: UnfinalizedYtRecord

udt_struct_v0.doc: One account's positions to seize in a batch. A zero field means "leave that position alone".
udt_struct_v0.name: SeizeRequest

udt_struct_v0.doc: The permanent trace of one recovery event for one account.
udt_struct_v0.name: RecoveryRecord

fields.doc: Set by `finalize_record`: the underlying the held PT and YT settled into.
fields.name: finalized

fields.doc: LP seized, and what the pool paid out for it: PT (held), SY shares and their underlying.
fields.name: lp_amount

fields.doc: PT seized directly / YT seized, held in escrow until `finalize_record`.
fields.name: pt_amount

fields.doc: SY shares seized directly, and the underlying they unwrapped to.
fields.name: sy_shares

fields.doc:
Yield the seized YT had already accrued (underlying units, before the YT fee). It moves to
the escrow's pending claim with the position, so it is recovered rather than stranded on a
deauthorized account. Exact per record. Yield accruing *after* the seizure is pooled by
the escrow's own holding address, not per record -- which is exactly why only one
unfinalized YT record is ever allowed to exist at a time (see the module doc's "At most
one unfinalized YT record at a time" section): with that guard in place, this record is
always the sole contributor to the pool between seizure and `finalize_record`, so
`underlying_from_yt` is exact too, not just `yt_yield_at_seize`.
fields.name: yt_yield_at_seize

function_v0.doc:
Permissionless keeper call: extend this contract's *instance* storage (admin, config,
reserves, totals, settlement rate, fee buckets) for ~30 days. Soroban does not bump instance
TTL on ordinary reads or writes, so a long-dated market needs this called periodically (or
an archived instance restored) -- see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
function_v0.name: bump

function_v0.doc: Seize `amount` of `account`'s LP: burn it in the pool for PT + SY, unwrap the SY leg at once\nand hold the PT leg. Writes a record; returns `(pt_received, underlying_from_sy_leg)`.
function_v0.name: seize_lp

function_v0.doc: Seize `amount` of `account`'s PT, held here until `finalize_record`. Writes a record.
function_v0.name: seize_pt

function_v0.doc: Seize `shares` of `account`'s SY and unwrap it into raw underlying held here, ready for the\nissuer's native clawback. `caller` must be the issuer authority; `account` must already be\ndeauthorized. Writes a recovery record; returns the underlying recovered.
function_v0.name: seize_sy

function_v0.doc: Seize `amount` of `account`'s YT, held here until `finalize_record`. Writes a record.
function_v0.name: seize_yt

function_v0.doc:
One-time wiring. Every position contract (and the manager and pool) must report the same
underlying as `underlying`. `caller` must be the live issuer authority for `underlying`
(the same standing every other market-creation `initialize` in this codebase already
requires) -- without this, deployment and initialization being necessarily separate
transactions left a window where anyone could front-run the legitimate operator's own
`initialize` call with attacker-controlled sub-contracts that merely echo the right
`underlying_address()`, permanently hijacking this instance (`AlreadyInitialized` blocks
any correction afterward) and silently no-opping every future seizure. Found during a
follow-up review after this contract's first audit pass; closes the same root-cause class
as C-1/M-12, on a window `scripts/create_market.sh`'s own two-step deploy-then-initialize
genuinely leaves open today.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc: Seize several accounts' positions in one transaction. The issuer is authenticated once;\nevery account is still individually checked for deauthorization, and one record is written\nper account. Reverts as a whole if any account is still authorized. Returns the record ids.
function_v0.name: seize_batch

function_v0.doc: Ids of every recovery record written for `account`, oldest first.
function_v0.name: account_records

function_v0.doc: Settle the PT and YT a record still holds (`pt_amount + lp_pt` PT and `yt_amount` YT) into\nthe underlying, at or after maturity, and write the result onto that record. Only the issuer\nauthority; once per record. Returns `(underlying_from_pt, underlying_from_yt)`.
function_v0.name: finalize_record

function_v0.doc: Seize *everything* the listed accounts hold across SY, PT, YT and LP, in one transaction.\nAccounts with no positions are skipped; reverts `NothingToSeize` if none had any.
function_v0.name: seize_all_positions
